newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania gives wage indexations in first half 1997.
newsitem.headline: Romania gives wage indexations in first half 1997.

text.p: Romania's centrist government, facing soaring inflation this year as it advances with its reforms, said on Tuesday it would offer wage indexations to cover around 75 percent of expected price rises.
Wage indexation will amount to 30.75 percent for the first quarter of this year and to 18.35 percent for the second quarter a government statement said.

The first-quarter indexation would cover 75 percent of the rise in consumer prices. The level for the second quarter would partially cover a forecast price rise of 22.7 percent against the first three months of the year.
The decision was made at the end of talks with leaders of trade unions, the statement said. Income taxes would be adjusted in order not to affect workers' take-home pay.

Romania expects year-on-year inflation to quicken to 89.5 percent this year from 56.9 percent in 1996. The government estimates first-quarter inflation of 41 percent, led by the freeing of prices for fuel, electricity and food.

But reforms agreed with international lenders last month aim to slash inflation to an annualised rate of around 30 percent in the second half of 1997. Romania is seeking $1.0 billion in fresh credits from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
